task.goal: Make a makerspace's shared 3D printer failures easier to diagnose before wasting a full print.
hard_constraints: Keep the existing printer and approved materials; no firmware changes or extra sensors.
Do not bypass the enclosure or normal ventilation and burn precautions.
Differentiate setup, material and machine causes using at most three small test prints and record time and material use.
task.available_resources: Printer log, sample filament, existing calibration card and operator checklist.
task.expected_result: A short fault-isolation process suitable for novice operators.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Controlled substitution: change setup, then filament
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Use a fixed small calibration coupon to isolate causes by changing one factor at a time. Print 1 establishes a baseline with the suspect filament and current settings, after checking that operation is safe. If it fails, use the existing checklist and calibration card to correct setup only; print 2 repeats the same file with the same filament. If it still fails, print 3 repeats the corrected setup using sample filament of the same approved material type and compatible specifications. Stop early when the evidence is sufficient.

A baseline failure followed by a pass after setup correction supports a setup cause. Failure after correction followed by a pass with sample filament supports a material or spool-feed cause. Failure in all three leaves a machine fault or an unresolved common setup/file problem; label this 'machine inspection needed,' not 'machine confirmed.' Multiple simultaneous faults remain possible.

Implementation needs one existing, previously successful small calibration file, a three-row record, the printer log, calibration card, checklist and sample filament. The sample must have documented successful use and suitable storage; otherwise it is an uncertain control. Define pass/fail from the card before printing. Record each intervention, observed defect, elapsed printing and handling time, and slicer-estimated material including purge and supports. Mark estimates explicitly. Keep enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions unchanged; unsafe symptoms end testing immediately.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: On the next naturally occurring failed job, compare this process with the initial diagnosis a novice would make from the existing checklist alone. A maintainer reviews the three records and subsequent routine inspection without running additional diagnostic prints. The smallest useful check is whether the controlled change yields a defensible cause category before attempting the full job. If the initial baseline already passes, record 'failure not reproduced.' If the reference filament or repeated file is unreliable, the process fails its isolation check rather than earning a machine diagnosis.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Use the printer's own history as the diagnostic control
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Diagnose departures from a documented successful configuration before making experimental changes. From the printer log, find a recent successful small calibration print using the existing calibration card. Compare its recorded setup, approved filament and maintenance context with the failed job. A novice worksheet marks differences as setup, material or machine-related, and identifies missing information. This works by using an established successful combination as the control, potentially avoiding a diagnostic print altogether when a clear setup discrepancy is found.

When printing is necessary, print 1 reproduces that reference configuration using suitable sample filament. If it passes, print 2 retains the reference setup but uses the suspect filament. Failure supports a material or spool-feed problem. If print 2 passes, print 3 uses the suspect job's setup on the same small geometry, changing only settings that the calibration card permits and that remain safe. Failure supports a setup cause; a pass leaves the original failure unexplained, including possible model-specific or intermittent causes. If print 1 fails, do not proceed through the filament comparison: inspect the log and checklist for changed setup or maintenance conditions and refer unresolved cases for machine inspection.

Resources are a sufficiently detailed success log, its saved file/settings, calibration card, checklist and approved sample filament. Without a reproducible reference, this alternative is unsuitable. A reference failure cannot distinguish machine trouble from an overlooked setup change. Record every print's settings, filament, result, elapsed time and estimated material, including purge. Count abandoned prints toward the three-print maximum. All enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions remain in force.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Apply the worksheet to one upcoming failure that has an adequate historical reference. Before testing, record the cause suggested by simply reading the most recent failure log as the comparator. Check whether the reference-based sequence narrows that assessment with observable pass/fail evidence within three small prints. A maintainer checks the classification during normal follow-up. Failure to reproduce the historical success without an identifiable change falsifies the assumption that the historical reference is a usable control; report an unresolved case rather than forcing a diagnosis.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Locate the failing print stage with targeted diagnostic shapes
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Use a short decision tree that tests different printing functions, rather than repeating one coupon with substituted settings or filament. The mechanism is to localize the defect: bed contact, sustained extrusion, or directional movement. This can expose problems before committing to a full job, although some symptoms have several possible causes.

First, use the operator checklist and printer log to look for direct evidence: a setting outside the calibration card, an incorrectly routed spool, recorded material-handling problems, or overdue machine attention. Correct mandatory setup items before testing; never deliberately reproduce unsafe conditions.

Run only the relevant branches, with three small prints as the absolute maximum:
1. A thin first-layer patch checks adhesion and line consistency against the calibration card. A documented setup discrepancy plus a passing patch after correction supports a setup cause.
2. A small hollow tower checks whether extrusion remains consistent after the first layer. Intermittent extrusion accompanied by visible filament damage or material symptoms identified by the existing card supports a material concern. Compare the unheated suspect filament visually with the sample, but do not treat appearance alone as proof.
3. A small square frame with straight runs in both bed directions checks whether errors consistently affect one movement direction. Repeated directional displacement with correct setup supports referral for machine inspection.

Stop when evidence supports an action. Mixed or ambiguous findings receive 'unresolved—maintainer review'; a tower failure alone does not establish bad filament. Passing these tests cannot exclude long-duration, model-specific or intermittent faults.

Implementation needs three simple geometries prepared in the existing slicer, approved card settings, and a one-page worksheet linking observations to actions. The card must provide usable acceptance criteria; otherwise a maintainer must define them before novice use. Record each started or aborted print, settings, observations, print and handling time, and estimated material including purge. Keep the enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions unchanged; unsafe symptoms end testing.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: For one naturally occurring failure, record a novice's checklist-only diagnosis, then apply the targeted sequence. Have a maintainer inspect the observations and ordinary follow-up findings. The smallest useful success is a supported category or a clearly justified referral within three small prints. A confident category contradicted by inspection, or observations that do not narrow the checklist-only assessment, counts against the method. No effectiveness result is yet established.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Compare the actual job’s instructions with its first printed layers
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Use a short prefix of the intended job as a conformance check: determine whether the defect is already present in the printing instructions or appears when the printer executes them. This targets job-specific failures that generic calibration shapes can miss.

Before printing, compare the existing job preview and settings with the calibration card and operator checklist. Look for unsupported starting features, missing contact with the bed, incorrect scale or orientation, and settings incompatible with the approved material. A visible defect in the instructions supports a setup cause. Correct it before proceeding.

Next, follow the checklist’s permitted inspection steps. Record material evidence separately from machine evidence: for example, visibly tangled or broken filament versus an observable damaged machine component. Novices should report observations rather than infer that every extrusion problem means bad filament. Unsafe findings stop the process and require a maintainer.

Print only the first few layers of the actual job, using the normal controls to stop at a predefined checkpoint. Choose a prefix small enough to limit consumption; if the job has a large footprint, this method is unsuitable. Compare the result with the preview and calibration card. A corrected instruction defect followed by a matching print supports setup; direct material evidence supports material handling action; correct instructions with unexplained physical deviation require machine inspection, without claiming a confirmed machine fault. Mixed evidence remains unresolved. Use one trial by default; any repeat after an identified correction counts toward an absolute maximum of three starts.

Implementation needs access to the job’s existing slicer preview, a short worksheet, and the supplied resources. Preview access is an assumption. Record elapsed printing and handling time, plus estimated material including purge and aborted work. Retain all enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions. Passing the prefix cannot exclude later failures.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: On one naturally occurring failed job, record a novice’s checklist-only assessment, then apply this process. A maintainer checks whether the preview defect or directly observed physical problem supports the assigned category. The method fails this initial check if it produces a confident category from ambiguous extrusion symptoms or the prefix does not exercise the reported failure. Its smallest useful success is a supported correction or justified referral before restarting the full job; no effectiveness is established yet.

EXPAND.title: Locate the defect with a spatial witness print
EXPAND.proposal:
Use where a defect appears to distinguish causes, rather than substituting settings and filament in sequence. A designated maintainer prepares one small file containing three identical first-layer patches at separated, safely reachable bed positions, followed by short walls. Use the calibration card’s approved settings and acceptance criteria. This requires an existing slicer and someone able to prepare the file; if unavailable, this route is unsuitable.

Before printing, a novice checks the operator checklist and log for unsafe conditions or obvious setup discrepancies. Correct documented discrepancies and record them. Print the witness file with the suspect approved filament, observing only through normal safe viewing arrangements. A defect confined to one bed region suggests local bed/setup trouble; interruptions occurring across positions suggest a shared extrusion or material problem. Neither pattern alone proves a cause.

Choose the next test from that evidence. For a localized defect, translate the same small layout within safe printable limits: a defect staying at the physical location supports a bed or machine issue; one following the geometry supports a file/setup issue. For widespread extrusion defects, repeat with compatible approved sample filament: improvement supports a material/feed cause. A third small print may verify one checklist-authorized correction. Count aborted starts toward the limit. Unclear or persistent failures go to the maintainer for machine inspection, with the location map and log; resume normal work only after routine clearance.

Record each print’s elapsed time, handling time, and slicer-estimated material including purge. Keep enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions unchanged. The mechanism exposes location-dependent faults that a single coupon could miss; intermittent faults and multiple simultaneous causes remain unresolved.
EXPAND.experiment: For the first suitable failure, the maintainer owns a trial capped at three small prints. Compare the location-based diagnosis with the conclusion obtainable from the prior controlled-substitution route’s single-coupon observations. Stop for unsafe symptoms or ambiguous evidence after the cap. Check whether spatial evidence changes a defensible next action, while comparing total time and material estimates. If it adds printing and interpretation without improving localization, prefer the simpler substitution route.

EXPAND.title: Gate the actual job with a short diagnostic prefix
EXPAND.proposal:
Use the beginning of the intended job as the diagnostic specimen, preserving features that a generic calibration coupon might omit. A maintainer first compares the failed job’s slicer preview and settings with the existing calibration card and checklist. Record discrepancies involving approved material profile, first-layer placement, supports and bed contact. Correct only documented setup errors. This requires access to the existing slicer and job file; no firmware change is needed.

Prepare a short version of the actual job that ends after a few informative layers, using normal slicer controls and a normal print completion. Include the suspect footprint or early feature, but impose a small time/material cap before starting. If the relevant feature cannot be reached within that cap, hand off rather than claiming this route can diagnose it cheaply.

Print 1 uses that prefix with the suspect filament. If it passes, record that early behavior passed; later failures remain untested. If it fails, print 2 uses a small calibration specimen based on the existing card with the same filament and approved profile. Prefix failure with calibration success supports a job-specific setup/geometry problem. Failure of both warrants print 3: repeat the calibration specimen with compatible approved sample filament. Recovery supports a material/feed cause; continued failure requires machine inspection or further setup review, not a confirmed machine diagnosis.

The novice records the failed feature, observed defect, interventions, elapsed print and handling time, and estimated material including purge. Aborted prints count toward three. Unsafe symptoms stop testing immediately; enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions remain unchanged. A maintainer reviews unresolved records and authorizes normal recovery. The mechanism makes job-specific early failures visible, but cannot clear the whole print or establish the health of an uncertain sample filament.
EXPAND.experiment: The maintainer owns one trial on a failure involving an early job feature. Before testing, record what the prior controlled-substitution route would investigate using its generic coupon. Stop at three small prints, the preset resource cap, or any unsafe symptom. Compare whether the prefix exposes a consequential defect the generic coupon misses, and include prefix-preparation time and material in the comparison. If both routes support the same action and prefix preparation adds work, this alternative has shown no improvement.

EXPAND.title: Controlled substitution with a valid filament transition
EXPAND.proposal:
Source: “Controlled substitution: change setup, then filament.” Preserve its three-print sequence, but make clearance of the previous filament a prerequisite for interpreting the sample-filament result. Residual material or an incomplete reload can otherwise make the final comparison misleading.

The novice first checks safe operation, defines acceptance using the existing calibration card, and selects an existing small calibration file. Print 1 uses the suspect filament and current safe setup. After failure, correct checklist-defined setup discrepancies only; print 2 repeats the same file and filament. Recovery supports a setup cause. If it still fails, use compatible approved sample filament for print 3, keeping the corrected setup fixed.

Changed action: before print 3, the operator follows the existing approved unload/load and purge procedure and records whether its completion criteria were met. Do not invent a purge quantity or change temperatures beyond approved instructions. If no suitable procedure exists, the transition fails, or the sample lacks credible successful-use and storage history, stop: the material comparison is invalid and the cause remains unresolved. A successful sample print supports a material or spool-feed cause; another failure warrants machine inspection plus review of common setup/file problems, not a confirmed machine diagnosis.

Record each intervention, defect, print and handling time, and estimated material including loading purge, supports and abandoned starts. Count every started test toward three. A passing baseline means “failure not reproduced,” not clearance of the original full job. The novice retains the record for the person normally responsible for printer maintenance; pending review, stop the failed job. Enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions remain unchanged.

This adds a bounded transition check to the source route. It could prevent false machine referrals, but consumes purge material and cannot resolve intermittent or simultaneous faults.
EXPAND.experiment: On one naturally occurring failure that reaches the filament-change step, the operator records the diagnosis that would have followed from the source sequence before checking transition validity. Complete no more than three small prints, stopping immediately for unsafe symptoms or a failed approved loading procedure. The normal maintenance owner reviews whether the final comparison was interpretable and whether it justified the next action. Compare the resulting classification and total time/material with the source procedure, including extra purge. If transition validity cannot be established with existing instructions, the trial ends as unresolved; do not add a fourth print to rescue it.

EXPAND.title: Historical control with one bounded recovery attempt
EXPAND.proposal:
Source: “Use the printer’s own history as the diagnostic control.” Keep its successful historical configuration as the control, but add a recovery branch when the first reference print fails. The source otherwise hands off immediately even when a specific checklist-correctable discrepancy is found.

The novice selects a recent successful small calibration file with recorded settings and compatible approved sample filament. Check the log, calibration card and operator checklist before starting. If the saved configuration or credible sample is unavailable, this route is unsuitable: record the missing prerequisite and stop for normal maintenance review.

Print 1 reproduces the reference. If it passes, print 2 uses the suspect filament with the same setup. Failure supports a material/feed cause. If it passes, print 3 may use the suspect job’s safe, card-permitted settings on the same specimen; failure supports a setup cause. Three passes leave model-specific, later-stage and intermittent failures unresolved.

Changed action: if print 1 fails, the operator may make exactly one correction explicitly authorized by the existing checklist, provided a concrete discrepancy is found. Print 2 repeats the reference with the same sample filament. Recovery supports that setup discrepancy as a cause; print 3 may then check the suspect filament under the recovered setup. If no permitted correction is identifiable, the repeat fails, or safe operation is uncertain, stop and refer the record for machine inspection and common-setup review. Do not classify reference failure alone as machine failure.

The operator logs every started print, intervention, result, elapsed print and handling time, and estimated material including purge. The three-start limit applies across interruptions; an incomplete record ends testing rather than resetting the allowance. The operator retains responsibility for stopping the failed job until the usual maintenance owner accepts the handoff. Keep normal enclosure, ventilation and burn precautions.

The recovery branch can resolve an ordinary setup problem without an immediate handoff, at the cost of a repeat reference print and less remaining capacity to investigate job-specific settings.
EXPAND.experiment: Use one failure with a reproducible historical reference. Before starting, the operator records the next action under the source route. Run the applicable branch within three small starts; the usual maintenance owner reviews the record during normal follow-up. Check whether a failed reference followed by a documented correction produces useful evidence, and compare printing time, material and avoided or delayed handoff with the source route. Stop at unsafe symptoms, missing reference prerequisites or the print limit. If the correction does not restore the reference, preserve the unresolved classification rather than attempting further diagnostic prints.

EXPAND.title: Trace the failed print before making another specimen
EXPAND.proposal:
Use physical and recorded evidence from the existing failure as the first diagnostic mechanism, removing the assumption that diagnosis must begin with another print. This route suits visible setup or filament-path problems; it cannot exclude hidden machine faults.

At the next failed-job cleanup, the novice keeps the failed piece and uses the log, calibration card and operator checklist to trace the observed defect backward. Perform only inspections already allowed by the checklist, after the required cooldown and with normal enclosure and ventilation precautions. Do not dismantle components or handle hot or moving parts.

Assign a provisional category only when there is concrete evidence: a logged job/profile discrepancy supports setup; an observable spool snag, crossed winding or filament break supports material/feed; a machine error or visible damage goes to the usual maintenance owner for inspection. A rough surface, poor adhesion or interrupted extrusion alone is ambiguous and must not determine the category. Record competing explanations.

If exactly one safe, checklist-authorized correction follows from the evidence, the operator makes it and runs one small existing calibration print using card-defined acceptance criteria. A pass supports the proposed cause and correction; a failure stops the route and triggers maintenance review. If the first failure supplied no specific actionable evidence, skip printing and hand off. The route uses at most one small test; abandoned starts count, and there are no retries within this process.

Record inspection and handling time, test time, and estimated material including purge; record zero new material when inspection alone ends the process. A passing coupon supports basic operation but does not clear unsupported geometry or later-stage behavior in the original job. The operator keeps the failed job stopped until the established correction or maintenance process permits resumption.

Resources are the existing failed piece, printer log, card and checklist. Compared with immediate coupon testing, this may avoid reproducing an obvious fault, but relies on observable evidence and may send more ambiguous cases to maintenance.
EXPAND.experiment: The operator and usual maintenance owner review three existing or naturally occurring cases: a clear checklist-authorized setup correction, a similar-looking case without supporting evidence, and an unfamiliar defect. Do not create faults. Check that only the first case triggers operator correction and a small verification print; ambiguous cases should retain uncertainty and reach the normal maintenance owner. Compare the proposed next action, inspection time and new material use with starting a generic coupon immediately. Stop any live trial for unsafe symptoms or after its single verification start. If the evidence rules repeatedly misclassify ambiguous cases, withdraw this route rather than expanding novice inspection authority.
